handbookNote: Primary source: the official 'Hawaii Driver's Manual' (2023 edition, internally dated HMG 5/2023), State of Hawaii Department of Transportation, Highways Division, fetched directly from hidot.hawaii.gov/highways/files/2024/11/2023-Hawaii-Drivers-Manual_5.375x8.375_Final-r3-Digital-071924web.pdf on 2026-08-16 (full text extracted to temp/handbooks/hi/driver.txt, 5083 lines / ~318KB). This is the single statewide manual used for the knowledge test; the manual's own cover page states it 'INCLUDES Complete Test Questions and Answers From State of Hawaii Dept. Of Transportation.' County-administration structure CONFIRMED and documented: Hawaii's driver licensing is administered locally by the four County Driver Licensing offices (City & County of Honolulu, County of Hawaii, County of Kauai, County of Maui) rather than a single statewide DMV -- each county schedules and proctors its own written and road tests -- but all four counties use one common statewide manual (this document) and, per hidot.hawaii.gov and honolulu.gov, a single shared online knowledge-test platform (knowtodrive.com/hawaii, operated by Intellectual Technology Inc.) that lists per-county fees for Honolulu, Hawaii, Kauai and Maui counties alike. Real exam mechanics CONFIRMED (not borrowed from any other state): the Category 3 (car) written knowledge test is a 30-question test -- confirmed independently on three official honolulu.gov pages (Driver's License FAQ, Driver's License Procedures, and the Online Learner's Permit Test FAQ) plus the shared statewide testing vendor page, all fetched 2026-08-16. The online version of the test carries a 60-minute (one-hour) time limit; the in-person version's time limit is not stated on any official source found, so that detail is left unconfirmed rather than guessed. The PASSING SCORE / minimum correct-answer threshold is NOT published on hidot.hawaii.gov, the Hawaii Driver's Manual, or any of the four county driver-licensing pages found after real research effort (Hawaii County and Kauai County's own sites blocked automated fetches outright) -- this is reported honestly as unconfirmed rather than invented or borrowed from another state's threshold. Content-depth rationale: this is an unusually rich, detailed statewide manual (full chapters on licensing/GDL, vehicle equipment/registration/insurance law, crash and financial-responsibility procedures, alcohol/drug law with specific BAC thresholds, a full traffic-signs/signals/pavement-markings chapter, right-of-way and roundabout rules, safe-driving and defensive-driving technique, a dedicated emergency-driving-procedures chapter covering skids/blowouts/brake and steering failure/freeway driving/weather, a large-vehicles-and-towing chapter, and dedicated pedestrian-safety and bicycle-safety chapters with Hawaii-specific statistics) plus an embedded official practice-question bank exceeding 170 numbered items -- comfortably supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded question pool. Price matches this project's established fixed Driver-track rate ($4.99), not a placeholder. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official manual text or a specific official honolulu.gov / knowtodrive.com page cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
